description: The SECOND `keyword`-carrying runtime site keeps the canonical identity too (issue #741). A `map` body is a value context, so an escape inside it raises `ol-return-in-comprehension` (`spec/execution-model.md:226-227`, `spec/error-model.md:116`) rather than `ol-return-outside-proc`, even at the top level — and the EXECUTED Heritage spelling `output` reports `params` `{ keyword: "return", form: "map" }`, byte-identical to the Core twin `tests/conformance/core-language/comprehensions/comprehension-return-in-comprehension` (`:out = map n in [1] [ return :n ]`, same `params`, same `stage: "semantic"`). This site is fixtured separately from the outside-proc one because the runtime carries a SEPARATE copy of the rule for it — the defect was present at both copies, and a fixture for only one would leave the other unpinned. `params` is canonical; the `message` still names what the learner typed. The `source_span` is the whole `output :n` escape statement — the runtime's own span for this rule, which is why identity is asserted on `code` + `params` and not on the span (`spec/error-model.md:255-260`). Issue #815: `execute()` now runs Layer 1 and Layer 2 before Phase 2 and refuses a program carrying an `error`-severity finding (`spec/execution-model.md:659-664`), so no event is emitted and the diagnostic delivered here is the CHECK's. The runtime's own copy of the rule still exists and still runs — under the `runUnchecked` opt-out — and is collapsed into the check's by the de-duplication rule (`spec/execution-model.md:741-748`), which is why only one report survives and it reads `stage: "semantic"`.
